top_choice_rationale: Cărtărescu (P001) is the only writer-centered proposal on the slate, and on the common criteria his case is the most complete. His voice is distinctive, built from long patterned sentences and recurring images of memory, the body and dream. As publicly described, Blinding (the Orbitor trilogy) and Solenoid carry formal ambition at the scale of whole architectures. That gives the prose imaginative and intellectual depth that does not rest on topicality, nationality or political symbolism. The citation scope is clean: one writer, one language, with prose as the load-bearing element and poetry named only as formative ground, since translation coverage of the poetry and early work is thin. Real uncertainties remain. I cannot judge Romanian rhythm and syntax through translation. Whether the late novels deepen the early project or partly repeat it is unresolved. I have not independently verified any text. These limits concern how fully the case can be tested and do not show a failure of any stated criterion. They are not strong enough to prefer no award (P000), which I rank last. The agreement among the six round-2 files is not treated as evidence of merit.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; the profile records co-election with David Håkansson (2023), a collaboration with Kate Larson, and work on Selma Lagerlöf, none of which is a documented tie to Cărtărescu. Disclosed, not adjudicated.
